narrative: Constructed 2026-08-29 as the worked example of the ATELIER language (the wider shelf). A fine-art wedding photographer with eleven strong images and almost no copy, who leads with the craft ('I shoot film, I wait for the light') and whose clients arrive curious, novice about photography, and wanting to feel they have found the expensive-quiet one. Fills library holes: craft_first + novice + curious + exclusive_premium + honor + discrete_artifacts, and the artifact_showcase hero on a light ground with tonal colour and no motion. Resulting direction: A QUIET GALLERY — bone ground, one image at a time in a wide mat, a thin serif at modest scale, tiny roman-numeral captions, one muted metal for the single line that matters. Teaches: the matted single-image hero, the gallery as the argument, captions as the only copy, centred formality without gravitas, and stillness as luxury.

evidence: their three verbs: Wait / See / Keep
I shoot film, I wait for the light
they don't know what film is; they know what it feels like
who it's for, in their words: couples who saw one of my photos somewhere and went looking
it's their day; I'm the one who was watching
they want visitors to feel: hushed, expensive, found
the fine-art wedding convention — bone ground, serif, big images — is kept and executed better
just my name in a serif, if that
they asked for a gallery of real work
waits, watches, keeps — the speech has the same pace

palette.because: P4: a light room the couple stands inside; a bone ground with tonal greys so the photographs carry all the colour; one muted metal for the single line that matters.

typography.pairing_logic: A thin serif at modest scale for the few lines there are, the same family italic for the one caption line — kinship, quiet; enabler_behind (P13) means the type never competes with the frame.
typography.because: The images are the display type; the words are captions.

layout.because: One image, centred, in a wide mat — the gallery convention honoured (P9) and executed with more air than anyone in the vertical.

motion.signature_move: none — the frames do not move; the visitor does
motion.because: P8/P12: stillness is the luxury; a deliberate speaker's gallery never slides.

hero_concept.concept_statement: One photograph in a wide bone mat with a hairline frame, a roman numeral beneath it, and a single italic line — 'I wait for the light.' Nothing else above the fold; the second image arrives as you scroll.
hero_concept.because: discrete_artifacts + craft_first → the work is the hero; the couple (P13) sees themselves in the frame, not the photographer.

whitespace.because: P2: the mat IS the confidence claim — 40% of every screen is bone.

notes: her three verbs become the three chapter captions — Wait, See, Keep — each under one image
prices are one line in the serif, no table, no tiers
the testimonial is two sentences in italic under the couple's own photograph
the contact block is a single sentence and a date field
voice_to_visual.because: A voice that says little becomes a page that shows much — captions carry the whole argument.

rule_break.what: the hero is a single photograph with a caption and no headline at all
rule_break.because: Even fine-art wedding sites lead with a name; leading with the work and a numeral is the one quiet break inside an honoured convention.

tension.expression: The hush owns the mats, the numerals, the stillness; the warmth owns the bone (not white), the italic captions in her voice and the couple's own photo above the testimonial.
tension.because: Hush alone reads as cold; warmth alone reads as cheap — the mat is warm-toned on purpose.

first_impression.feel_in_3s: I found the quiet, expensive one.
first_impression.remember: One photograph in a wide bone mat with a numeral under it.
first_impression.because: exclusive_premium for a curious novice = restraint they can feel without vocabulary.

language.because: Eleven real photographs, a craft-first quiet voice, a curious novice audience and an exclusive-premium feeling — the frame should be wide and still; Monograph would be too dark and Mural too loud for hush.

distinctiveness_check.notes: Nearest are e2 and e5 (light, serif, centred, still) but this is tonal not single-accent, an artifact hero not a typographic or environment one, and airy with no motion where e5 breathes — a gallery, not a room or a paper.

summary_for_practitioner: Your site is a quiet gallery. One photograph at a time, centred in a wide bone-coloured mat with a hairline frame and a small roman numeral under it — no headline, no slideshow, nothing moves. Your three words, Wait, See, Keep, become the three chapters, each under one image. The few lines of text are set in a thin serif, your prices are a single sentence, and the one testimonial sits in italics under that couple's own photograph. Forty percent of every screen is empty on purpose: that air is the expensive part.
